openings.claim: Hypothesis: immutable video-caption snapshots and hashes identify each request; completion order cannot change the editor-selected intended pair. Workers consume those snapshots; previews expose wording and video identity.
openings.discriminator: Correct selection with wrong actual input hashes implicates worker binding; reverse completion should preserve intended identity. Render duration need not improve.
openings.fit: Preserves private accounts, embedded delivery, and accessible last-delivered pair with original wording; feasibility within four engineer-days, one shared editor-day and 80 processing hours/week remains uncertain.
openings.probe: Privately stage fabricated footage, two cuts and repeated caption edits; force reverse completion. Both editors identify intended and last-delivered versions without worksheets; verify actual worker inputs and artifact hashes against requested pairs.
openings.uncertainty: Atomic binding, identification usability and snapshot costs unproven; observed mismatches are not causally linked to reverse completion.

openings.claim: Determine whether late sessions wait for the intended preview or lose time selecting, downloading and inspecting an available preview.
openings.discriminator: Readiness after minute 15 supports scheduling/render investigation, including redundant queued renders; earlier readiness followed by late identification supports identification/review investigation.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints if observation shares the editor-day; otherwise limit sampling.
openings.probe: Combine request/start/completion events with final-edit, intended-pair readiness, selection and verified-playback observations; compare repeated edits with single corrections.
openings.uncertainty: Intended pairs need independent verification. Nine successful single corrections limit a general bottleneck claim; demonstration behavior may differ. Festival capacity remains unknown.

decision: Probe both within shared allowances before choosing a speed intervention. Staging cannot establish success: assess 30 new sessions for at least 90% correct identification within 15 minutes and zero unintended-pair deliveries; limited sampling remains provisional.
